propositions.text: This is a judicial review of a visa officer's decision refusing Chi Kan Kwan's permanent resident visa application under the Start-up Business Class.
propositions.quote: This application for judicial review challenges a visa officer’s [the Visa Officer] decision dated June 28, 2018 refusing the application of Chi Kan Kwan for a permanent resident visa as a member of the Start-up Business Class.

propositions.text: The application was refused because it was found to be primarily for acquiring immigration status, not for engaging in authorized business activity.
propositions.quote: The stated basis for the decision was a finding that Ms. Kwan’s application for landing was primarily brought for the purpose of acquiring immigration status and not for the required purpose of engaging in an authorized business activity.

paragraphs.summary: The court reviews a visa officer's refusal of Chi Kan Kwan's application, which was denied for being primarily to gain immigration status, not business activity.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan's application met the initial technical requirements for the start-up business venture program.
propositions.quote: It is common ground that Ms. Kwan’s application met the initial technical requirements to qualify as a start-up business venture under the applicable program.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan needed to show intent to operate a business in Canada and have an agreement with a designated entity.
propositions.quote: Among other things, Ms. Kwan was required to demonstrate an intention to operate a business in Canada. It was also necessary for Ms. Kwan to enter into an agreement with a designated entity which would provide various forms of support to the proposed venture.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan entered an agreement with Empowered Startups Ltd., a Vancouver business incubator, for a financial website venture.
propositions.quote: In Ms. Kwan’s case, an agreement was reached with a designated business incubator based in Vancouver, namely Empowered Startups Ltd. [Empowered]. The agreement described the proposed joint venture as a fee based “one stop information platform (Financial Website)” linking Chinese investors with institutions offering Canadian financial products.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan met the program's technical requirements, including an agreement with Empowered Startups Ltd. for a financial website venture.

propositions.text: A concern arose about a possible conflicting venture supported by Empowered, raising doubts about Empowered's involvement in status acquisition.
propositions.quote: When Ms. Kwan’s application came up for initial review a concern was raised about a possible conflicting venture being supported by Empowered. The reviewing Visa Officer noted that this “raises concerns about possible [Empowered] involvement in assisting applicants in acquiring status or privilege under IRPA”.

propositions.text: The officer requested a peer review from CABI, which identified problems and noted significant changes to the business model.
propositions.quote: This concern led the officer to ask the Canadian Association of Business Incubation [CABI] for a peer review of the proposed business model. CABI’s peer review report dated February 16, 2018 identified problems with the proposal and noted that the business model had “changed significantly since the initial application was submitted”.

propositions.text: CABI's report stated Ms. Kwan committed to paying $300,000 for a year of incubation, which is not normal in Canada.
propositions.quote: The report also stated that Ms. Kwan “has committed to paying $300,000 for a year of incubation services. This is not normal for an incubator in Canada”.

paragraphs.summary: Concerns about Empowered's role led to a CABI peer review, which found problems and noted Ms. Kwan's unusual $300,000 incubation fee commitment.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan was asked twice for a status update on her business establishment and operation.
propositions.quote: On February 28, 2018, Ms. Kwan was asked to provide a status update on the establishment and operation of her business. This request was followed up with a second request on March 9, 2018.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan provided a three-page update describing a new business model involving a chatbot platform, explaining the initial model was abandoned due to regulation concerns.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan then provided a three page “Venture Update” describing a new business model involving a chatbot platform connecting financial institutions with potential customers. She also explained that the initial business model had been abandoned because of financial regulation concerns.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan was twice asked for a business update and responded with a new chatbot business model, citing regulatory concerns for abandoning the original plan.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan's update led to concerns about her seriousness, as outlined in the Visa Officer's file notes.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan’s update gave rise to a new concern about “lack of seriousness”. This is outlined in the following passage from the Visa Officer’s file notes:

propositions.text: The Visa Officer found Ms. Kwan's business venture changed significantly and lacked evidence of significant progress or seriousness.
propositions.quote: Upon review of the documents PA submitted, she has failed to provide sufficient evidence to demonstrate that she has made significant progress in the last year. I also note that Empowered Startups Ltd. has accepted and is investing in a business venture similar to her initial proposal which would have directly competed with her business. This is atypical of a venture capital investor. The lack of seriousness by PA and designated entity in entering the proposal leads me to conclude that her intentions were other than carrying out a business in Canada.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer concluded Ms. Kwan participated in the agreement primarily to acquire permanent residence, not to engage in the intended business activity.
propositions.quote: I therefore have concerns that PA has participated in an agreement or arrangement in respect of the commitment for the purpose of acquiring permanent residence in Canada and not for the purpose of engaging in the business activity for which the commitment was intended.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan's update raised concerns about her seriousness, leading the Visa Officer to conclude her intent was immigration, not business activity.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer sent Ms. Kwan a procedural fairness letter raising the same concerns and questioning the bona fides of her application, including lack of progress information.
propositions.quote: The Visa Officer followed up with a procedural fairness letter to Ms. Kwan raising all of the same concerns and questioning the bona fides of her application. Included in the letter was a specific concern about the lack of information provided about the progress of the venture during the previous year.

paragraphs.summary: The Visa Officer sent Ms. Kwan a procedural fairness letter raising concerns about her application's bona fides and lack of progress information.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan replied to the fairness letter, explaining the business model change, her work, and denying competition with Empowered's other venture.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan responded to the fairness letter in a four page reply and enclosed copies of her communications with the representatives from Empowered. Her reply explained the rationale behind the change to the business model and described the work that had gone into the new proposal. She claimed to have been actively engaged in the incubation process to the extent of “about” 10 hours of work per week. Ms. Kwan also explained that the work being done by Empowered in the development of another chatbot venture did not compete with her business idea.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan criticized the Visa Officer for second guessing her business decisions and threatened legal action if refused.
propositions.quote: Her letter concluded with a criticism that the Visa Officer was second guessing her business decisions and with a threat that she was exploring her legal options in the event of a negative decision.

propositions.text: Despite Empowered's involvement, Ms. Kwan did not provide any supporting material from Empowered with her response.
propositions.quote: It is of some significance that, despite Empowered’s significant involvement in the development of Ms. Kwan’s venture, nothing from that source was provided with her response.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan replied to the fairness letter, explaining her actions, denying competition, criticizing the officer, but provided no support from Empowered.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer concluded Ms. Kwan's application was primarily motivated by acquiring immigration status, not pursuing a legitimate business opportunity.
propositions.quote: Notwithstanding Ms. Kwan’s answers, the Visa Officer concluded that the application was primarily motivated by a desire to acquire immigration status in Canada and not to pursue a legitimate business opportunity.

paragraphs.summary: The Visa Officer concluded Ms. Kwan mainly sought immigration status, not a genuine business opportunity, despite her responses.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer reviewed Ms. Kwan's evidence and was not satisfied she was actively involved in developing her business or managing it from Canada.
propositions.quote: Based on the information provided by the PA, I am not satisfied that the PA has been in Canada exercising her work permit to develop her business venture. I am not satisfied that the PA will provide active and ongoing management of this business from within Canada.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer found that Empowered's representative, not Ms. Kwan, was developing the business and Ms. Kwan failed to provide sufficient evidence of her involvement.
propositions.quote: The chat logs (Appendix B) suggest that Chang of Empowered Startups Ltd. was developing the PA’s business venture and providing the PA with updates. According to the April 2, 2017 e-mail between the PA and Chang (Appendix A), it appears as though Chang created the survey questions. Furthermore, Chang built the company website as per the April 21, 2017 e-mail between the PA and Chang. Chang continued to make changes and develop the websites and informed the PA when to have her friends test the website. According to the February 20, 2018 e-mail, the PA did not hear from Chang on her venture. The PA has failed to provide sufficient evidence to satisfy me that she is actively involved in developing her business.

propositions.text: The Collaborative Research Agreement and related emails did not include Ms. Kwan or her business, and she was not copied on correspondence.
propositions.quote: Moreover, I note that the Collaborative Research Agreement was signed by UBC and Empowered (Appendix F). It did not include the PA or name her business venture. All e-mail correspondence provided took place between UBC and Empowered as well. I note that the PA was not CC’d on these e-mails (Appendix G).

propositions.text: The Visa Officer carefully considered Ms. Kwan's response but was not satisfied on the balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: The PA’s response to my PFL was carefully considered; however, it did not satisfactorily disabuse all of my concerns. Upon careful consideration of all information on file, I am not satisfied on the bal

paragraphs.summary: The Visa Officer found Ms. Kwan was not actively involved in her business, with most development done by Empowered, and her response was unconvincing.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan challenges the decision as unreasonable and procedurally unfair.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan challenges the reasonableness of the decision and argues, as well, that it is tainted by procedural unfairness.

propositions.text: The reasonableness issue is reviewed deferentially; procedural fairness is reviewed for correctness.
propositions.quote: The first issue attracts a deferential standard of review and the fairness issue must be examined for correctness.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan argues the decision was unreasonable and unfair; the court notes the standards of review for each issue.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan argues it was unreasonable for the officer to attribute improper purpose based solely on lack of business progress.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan asserts that it was unreasonable for the Visa Officer to attribute an improper purpose to her application based solely on a lack of progress in the development of her business.

propositions.text: The court finds this argument mischaracterizes the Visa Officer’s primary concern.
propositions.quote: This argument, however, mischaracterizes the Visa Officer’s primary concern.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan claims the officer's reasoning was unreasonable, but the court finds she mischaracterizes the officer's main concern.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer doubted Ms. Kwan's motives due to her lack of meaningful engagement in the business.
propositions.quote: It was Ms. Kwan’s lack of meaningful engagement in the development of the business that led the Visa Officer to doubt her motives.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan almost immediately returned to Hong Kong and did not provide active management from Canada, contrasting with her stated commitment.
propositions.quote: This concern is best reflected in the Visa Officer’s observation that Ms. Kwan had almost immediately returned to Hong Kong and had not provided active and ongoing management of the business from within Canada. This history of minimal engagement stands in stark contrast to Ms. Kwan’s stated commitment to the development of her business.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the officer doubted Ms. Kwan's motives due to her minimal engagement and immediate return to Hong Kong, contrary to her commitments.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan's Commitment Certificate stated she was essential, would be Director, primary shareholder, CEO, and work full-time in Vancouver.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan’s Commitment Certificate stated that she was “essential” to the business and would be a Director, the primary shareholder, and the Chief Executive Officer of the company to be incorporated. The Certificate also described Ms. Kwan’s operational role in considerable detail and stated that she would be employed in a full‑time position based in Vancouver working out of premises supplied by Empowered.

propositions.text: A work permit was requested for urgent business reasons for Ms. Kwan to assume employment in Canada.
propositions.quote: A work permit was also requested for “urgent business reasons” to permit Ms. Kwan to assume her employment responsibilities within Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan's Commitment Certificate described her as essential, with a full-time operational role in Vancouver, and a work permit was urgently requested.

propositions.text: Empowered provided a letter stating Ms. Kwan would attend and remain in Vancouver from January to December 2017.
propositions.quote: It is also noteworthy that Empowered provided a letter of support for the project stating that Ms. Kwan would “attend and remain located in Vancouver” between January 2017 and December 2017.

paragraphs.summary: Empowered stated Ms. Kwan would remain in Vancouver throughout 2017 in their letter of support.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan only stayed in Canada for one week, incorporated the business, met Empowered twice, then returned to Hong Kong and had minimal involvement.
propositions.quote: Notwithstanding these assurances and the issuance of a work permit on February 25, 2017, Ms. Kwan came to Canada for only one week between the dates of February 28, 2017 and March 7, 2017 after which she returned to Hong Kong and remained there. During her brief visit to Vancouver she incorporated the business and met twice with Empowered representatives. After that visit, Ms. Kwan’s active operational involvement in the business venture was limited to mostly cursory email and WeChat exchanges with representatives of Empowered.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan only spent one week in Canada, then returned to Hong Kong, with minimal further involvement in the business.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan reneged on her commitment to live in Vancouver and devote herself to the business, failing to inform authorities of her departure or business changes.
propositions.quote: This history shows that Ms. Kwan almost immediately reneged on her firm commitment to live in Vancouver and to devote her time and energy in Canada to her business. No effort was made to inform the visa authorities that Ms. Kwan had left Canada and was working from Hong Kong. Similarly, Ms. Kwan neglected to inform program officials in a timely way about the significant change that had been made to the business model.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan discussed these issues with Empowered via WeChat, as shown in the record.
propositions.quote: All of this is surprising in the face of Ms. Kwan’s WeChat exchanges with Empowered representatives about these issues and the advice she was given (see CTR at pages 158 and 163).

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Ms. Kwan reneged on her commitments, failed to inform authorities, and discussed these issues with Empowered via WeChat.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan argues the officer erred by assessing her motivations after the application date.
propositions.quote: I reject Ms. Kwan’s argument that the Visa Officer erred by assessing her motivations at a time subsequent to the application.

propositions.text: The court finds a good faith obligation continues beyond the application, justifying ongoing assessment of commitment and progress.
propositions.quote: In my view, a good faith obligation continues to exist beyond the initiation of an application under this program. If it were otherwise, no purpose would be served by requiring a commitment from the applicant going forward, for regular progress reporting, and for a post-application peer review.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan argues the officer erred by assessing later motives, but the court finds good faith obligations continue beyond the application date.

propositions.text: There is nothing in the decision suggesting Ms. Kwan's motives were assessed only after her application; past motives can be assessed by later conduct.
propositions.quote: There is nothing in the Visa Officer’s decision suggesting that Ms. Kwan’s motives were ascertained at some point subsequent to the date of her application. A person’s past motivations can be reasonably assessed by examining their subsequent behaviour and clearly that was what happened here.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan's initial motives were questioned due to her immediate failure to fulfill her operational commitments.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan’s initial motives were questioned based on her almost immediate failure to live up to the clear commitments she had given about the details of her intended operational involvement.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the officer assessed Ms. Kwan's motives based on her immediate failure to fulfill commitments, not on later events alone.

propositions.text: Ministerial Instruction 7 excludes applicants who intend or have participated in a commitment primarily for immigration status.
propositions.quote: Ministerial Instruction 7 provides that an applicant will not be considered a member of the start-up business class “if they intend to participate, or have participated, in an agreement or arrangement in respect of a commitment primarily for the purpose of acquiring [immigration] status”.

propositions.text: This language contradicts Ms. Kwan's argument that there is a temporal limitation on assessing motives.
propositions.quote: This language belies Ms. Kwan’s argument that a temporal limitation applied to the assessment of her motives.

paragraphs.summary: Ministerial Instruction 7 allows assessment of motives at any time, contradicting Ms. Kwan's argument for a temporal limitation.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer's finding of lack of bona fide intent was reasonable; Ms. Kwan failed to honor her commitments and showed minimal business activity.
propositions.quote: I am satisfied that the Visa Officer’s finding of a lack of a bona fide intent on the part of Ms. Kwan was reasonable. While it may well be open to applicants in Ms. Kwan’s situation to hold back from initiating business activity until permanent residency has been obtained, that is not what Ms. Kwan did. She gave clear commitments that she failed to honour and the level of her business activity was minimal at best.

propositions.text: The problem was Ms. Kwan's lack of engagement, not Empowered's involvement; the officer could reasonably conclude she was not serious about the business.
propositions.quote: The problem was not that Empowered was actively engaged with the business venture but, rather the problem was that Ms. Kwan was not. On this record it was open to the Visa Officer to conclude that Ms. Kwan was not serious about the business and was instead primarily seeking immigration status.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the officer's conclusion reasonable: Ms. Kwan failed to honor commitments, showed minimal activity, and was not serious about the business.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer relied on extrinsic evidence (CABI peer review report) about Ms. Kwan's $300,000 commitment to Empowered.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan’s fairness argument is based on a reference in the CABI peer review report to the atypical commitment by Ms. Kwan to pay $300,000 to Empowered for its support during the first year of the start-up.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer had a duty to bring this extrinsic evidence to Ms. Kwan's attention.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan contends that the Visa Officer must have taken this extrinsic evidence into account and, therefore, had a duty to bring it to her attention.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer's real reason for rejection was concern about Empowered's motivations, not Ms. Kwan's.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan argues that the Visa Officer’s actual rationale for rejecting her application had more to do with a concern about Empowered’s motivations than hers.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer's file note and procedural fairness letter did not fully address this concern.
propositions.quote: This suspicion, she says, was also reflected in the Visa Officer’s file note of September 12, 2017 – a concern that was not fully addressed in the Visa Officer’s procedural fairness letter.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan argues the Visa Officer relied on extrinsic evidence and undisclosed concerns about Empowered, which should have been disclosed to her.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer initially had concerns about Empowered's business model and motives, and Ms. Kwan was not told about this issue.
propositions.quote: I accept Ms. Kwan’s point that the Visa Officer harboured an initial concern about Empowered’s business model and its motives. It is also apparent that Ms. Kwan was not told about the issue.

propositions.text: There is nothing in the decision indicating Empowered's conduct was ultimately considered in rejecting Ms. Kwan's application.
propositions.quote: there is nothing in the Visa Officer’s decision indicating that Empowered’s conduct was ultimately taken into account in the rejection of Ms. Kwan’s application.

propositions.text: The stated basis for rejection was Ms. Kwan's lack of meaningful operational involvement, which was a reasonable justification.
propositions.quote: The stated basis for the decision was Ms. Kwan’s lack of meaningful operational involvement with the start-up and that was, on its own, a reasonable justification for the decision.

propositions.text: There is no basis to conclude the Visa Officer had a disguised motive for the decision.
propositions.quote: On this record, there is simply no basis to conclude that the Visa Officer harboured some disguised motive for the decision.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer likely accepted Ms. Kwan's explanation for Empowered's assistance and dispelled the conflict of interest concern.
propositions.quote: if an inference is to be drawn it would be that Ms. Kwan’s explanation for Empowered’s assistance to a similar venture was accepted and the Visa Officer’s conflict of interest concern was dispelled.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Visa Officer's initial concerns about Empowered were not part of the rejection, which was based on Ms. Kwan's lack of involvement.

propositions.text: There was no requirement to inform Ms. Kwan about the Visa Officer's initial concerns since they were not a factor in the decision.
propositions.quote: In the absence of evidence that the Visa Officer’s initial concerns about Empowered were a factor in the decision, there was no requirement to bring that issue to Ms. Kwan’s attention.

propositions.text: This case is different from Sapojnikov, where a failure to disclose a 'poison pen' letter was at issue.
propositions.quote: This situation is very different from the case of Sapojnikov v Canada (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship), 2017 FC 964, 285 ACWS (3d) 153, involving a failure to disclose a “poison pen” letter received one day before the sending of a procedural fairness letter.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no duty to disclose the initial concerns, distinguishing this case from Sapojnikov where undisclosed evidence was relevant.

propositions.text: In Sapojnikov, the letter impugned the applicant's credibility and was likely a factor in the decision to send a procedural fairness letter.
propositions.quote: The content of the letter directly impugned the applicant’s credibility and Justice Anne Mactavish drew an inference that it must have been a factor in the decision to send the procedural fairness letter.

propositions.text: There was a duty to disclose the letter to the applicant in Sapojnikov.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, there was a duty to disclose the letter to the applicant.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains that in Sapojnikov, the undisclosed letter affected credibility and triggered a duty to disclose, unlike in Ms. Kwan's case.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer's reservations about Empowered were irrelevant to Ms. Kwan's motives or credibility.
propositions.quote: the Visa Officer’s tentative reservations about Empowered had no relevance to the assessment of Ms. Kwan’s motives or her credibility.

propositions.text: CABI's reference to Ms. Kwan's $300,000 commitment was never pursued by the Visa Officer.
propositions.quote: CABI’s reference to Ms. Kwan’s $300,000 commitment to Empowered was, not surprisingly, never taken up by the Visa Officer as a point of subsequent interest.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Visa Officer's concerns about Empowered and the $300,000 commitment were irrelevant and not considered in the decision.

propositions.text: The application is dismissed for the reasons given.
propositions.quote: For the foregoing reasons, this application is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses Ms. Kwan's application.

propositions.text: Neither party proposed a certified question and no issue of general importance arises.
propositions.quote: Neither party proposed a certified question and no issue of general importance arises on this record.

propositions.text: The application is dismissed as per the court's judgment.
propositions.quote: THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that this application is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes no certified question was proposed and formally dismisses the application in its judgment.
